classification.difficultyReason: Find interest from the growth in value, then substitute into the simple-interest formula and solve for the annual rate.

content.prompt: At what rate of simple interest will:

children.label: a
children.prompt: $\$10\,000$ grow to $\$14\,000$ over a five-year period?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}I&=14\,000-10\,000\\I&=4000\end{align*}$$
Using $I=PRT$ with $T$ in years:
$$\begin{align*}4000&=10\,000\times R\times5\\R&=\frac{4000}{50\,000}\\R&=0.08\\R&=8\%\end{align*}$$
The rate is $8\%$ p.a.

children.label: b
children.prompt: $\$8000$ grow to $\$10\,000$ over a two-year period?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}I&=10\,000-8000\\I&=2000\end{align*}$$
Using $I=PRT$ with $T$ in years:
$$\begin{align*}2000&=8000\times R\times2\\R&=\frac{2000}{16\,000}\\R&=0.125\\R&=12\frac{1}{2}\%\end{align*}$$
The rate is $12\frac{1}{2}\%$ p.a.

children.label: c
children.prompt: $\$1500$ grow to $\$2000$ over a three-year period?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}I&=2000-1500\\I&=500\end{align*}$$
Using $I=PRT$ with $T$ in years:
$$\begin{align*}500&=1500\times R\times3\\R&=\frac{500}{4500}\\R&=\frac{1}{9}\\R&=11\frac{1}{9}\%\end{align*}$$
The rate is $11\frac{1}{9}\%$ p.a.
